title: Sunscreen SPF50

drivers.name: Heatwave (38°C) + price increase
drivers.evidence: Price rose 4.1% (from $13.38 to $13.93) during a 38°C heatwave. No prior price increase with heat. Past promotions show noise-adjusted x1.02 lift; this is a unique, high-impact event. One past heatwave (2024) had no price change. Evidence is limited, so shrink toward 1.0.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 25.1. Halloween (event week) shows a noise-adjusted x1.0 effect, so no lift. However, a 4.1% price increase to $13.93 (from $13.38) coincides with a heatwave forecast of 38°C. Past promotions show a median lift of x1.23, but noise-adjusted x1.02. This price increase is deeper than prior promotions (max 30% off) and occurs in extreme heat—unlike past events. The heatwave likely drives demand beyond the baseline, but evidence is limited to one past occurrence of heat with no price change. The classical model’s x1.00 is too low. Adjust up with caution, shrinking toward 1.0 due to thin evidence. The baseline already captures seasonal trends (trend_13 = -21.9%), so no further trend adjustment. No pantry-loading risk, as no recent promotion.
